panels.label: Welcome
panels.title:
When the rules change,
can you ==change==?
panels.lede: The Money Table · Philippine Cashflow Club
panels.notes:
[Before you go live: audio, camera and chat tested. Your team is ready to drop the link and welcome names.]
[Stay silent for three seconds. Smile. Then read the line slowly.]
SAY: "When the rules change... can you change?"
[PAUSE]
SAY: "Good evening, everyone, and welcome to The Money Table with the Philippine Cashflow Club. That one question is the heart of everything we do. By the end of today, you will know your answer."
[2 min]
[Photo: a real Money Table game in progress.]

panels.label: Cameras on
panels.title: Cameras on. Write where you are from in the chat.
panels.notes:
SAY: "Before we start, three quick things. Cameras on, please. In the chat, write the city you are joining from. And keep yourself on mute when you are not speaking."
[Read three or four names aloud as they appear. Make them feel seen.]
SAY: "Manila, Cebu, Davao, Dubai, wow. We are all one room tonight."
ROOM MOVE: chat word = your city. [2 min]

panels.label: Three rules
panels.title: Three rules for today.

cards.title: Play along in the chat
cards.body: When I ask, you type. It keeps us all in the game.

cards.title: An offer is coming
cards.body: At the end I will share the next step. You decide.

panels.notes:
SAY: "Three simple rules. One: stay to the end, because the best part comes last. Two: play along in the chat. When I ask, you type, so we stay in the game together. Three: at the end, I will share a next step with you. You decide if it is for you."
SAY: "Is that okay with everyone? Write OK in the chat."
ROOM MOVE: chat word = OK. [Read out a few OKs.] [2 min]

panels.label: The promise
panels.title: By the end, you will know your next step on the ==money ladder==.
panels.notes:
SAY: "Here is my promise. By the end of this session, you will know your next step on the money ladder."
SAY: "The ladder is simple: Guest, Regular Member, VIP, then Gold. Every one of you is standing on one of those steps right now. We will find yours."
[Do not sell yet. Just plant the ladder.] [1 min]

panels.label: Smile
panels.caption: Smile.
panels.notes:
[Show the group photo from a past Money Table event.]
SAY: "Before we continue, look at this room. These are real people, from a real Money Table. Smile. You are part of this community now."
[Smile. Take a screenshot or photo of your own audience if you can.] [1 min]

panels.label: The problem
panels.title: Most people play to win a round. Few learn to change.
panels.notes:
SAY: "Let me tell you what I have seen, game after game. A player sits down. They play small deals, they build some capital, they wait for the big deal, and they get out of the Rat Race. They feel great."
SAY: "But here is the problem. Life does not keep the rules the same. Most people play to win one round. Very few learn to change."
SAY: "So I ask you: how many of you realise the rules of money are changing? Write ME in the chat."
ROOM MOVE: chat word = ME. [3 min]

panels.label: Two ways to play
panels.title:
You can wait for the Big Deal.
Or you can ==learn to adapt==.
new: Change your play when the rules change
panels.notes:
SAY: "So there are two ways to play. You can wait for the Big Deal, same strategy every time, hoping the right card appears, and getting stuck when the rules change."
SAY: "Or you can learn to adapt. Build capital with small deals. Pay down your liabilities. Change your play when the rules change."
SAY: "This is exactly what we teach at the Graduation Game. We do not give the answer. We guide you to discover it. Which side are you on tonight?"
[3 min]

panels.label: The low point
panels.title: The Big Deal cards are gone. Now what?
panels.sub: That moment is where players grow.
panels.notes:
[Lower your voice. Look into the camera.]
SAY: "Picture this. You have played this game many times. You know your strategy by heart. Then the facilitator reaches over, and removes every Big Deal card."
[PAUSE. Three seconds.]
SAY: "Now what?"
SAY: "In that moment, people feel it. Frustration. Fear. Some say, 'This is not fair.' And that moment is exactly where they grow."
«CONFIRM: if you have a true story of a real player, tell it here in your own words. Use a first name only with their permission.»
[3 min]

panels.label: Value by comparison
panels.title: Value is measured by ==comparison==.
panels.notes:
SAY: "Let me teach you one lesson right now. It takes two minutes. Value is measured by comparison."
SAY: "A deal is never good or bad by itself. It is good or bad compared to the other choices you have. Ask the room: which is better, a deal that earns eight percent, or one that loses money? Obvious, right? Let us make it harder."
[2 min]

panels.label: Good deal or bad deal
panels.title: A shopping mall at ==-24% ROI== is not a good Big Deal.
panels.notes:
SAY: "In our game there is a shopping mall. It looks like a Big Deal. It is big, it sounds impressive. But at minus 24 percent ROI, it is not a good deal."
SAY: "Big does not mean good. Would you buy it? Write YES or NO."
ROOM MOVE: chat word = YES or NO. [Read a few answers.]
SAY: "Size is not the measure. Return is the measure."
[3 min]

panels.label: Your turn
panels.title: Write one deal you passed on. Was it really a bad deal?
panels.notes:
SAY: "Your turn. You have three minutes. Think of one deal you passed on in real life. Was it really a bad deal, or did you just not know how to measure it? Write it down."
[Give three minutes of silence. Then ask two or three people to share. Optional: ask everyone to stand and stretch before moving on.] [3 min]

panels.label: The result
panels.title: You just practised the skill the ladder is built on.
panels.notes:
SAY: "Beautiful. You just practised the skill the whole ladder is built on. That is one skill. In the club, we teach many, one game at a time, with people who play next to you."
[1 min]

panels.label: Thank you
panels.title: Thank you for playing along.
panels.notes:
SAY: "Thank you for playing along. Thank you for being honest in the chat and trying things you were not sure about."
[Name two or three people who took part.]
[Smile.] [1 min]

panels.label: Permission
panels.ask: Would it be okay if I shared a small offer with you?
panels.notes:
SAY: "Now, I told you at the start that I would share an offer. So I am asking permission. Would it be okay if I shared a small offer with you? No pressure, and it takes just a few minutes. If it is okay, write OK in the chat."
[Wait. Read every OK. Anyone who does not answer is not ready, and that is fine.]
ROOM MOVE: chat word = OK. [2 min]
